R316.note: ProcessBuilder with a real argument array plus a leading-dash/character allowlist closes both command and argument injection; the allowed charset matches valid hostname syntax so legitimate hosts still pass.

R317.note: Per-category method allowlist restricts dynamic dispatch to the one declared safe method (send), matching the only real handler API and closing the arbitrary-method-invocation vector.

R318.note: HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode is applied to both untrusted values before concatenation, closing the reflected XSS with no other observable change (the 'Source' section confusingly shows the already-fixed code, but the delivered fix itself is correct).

R319.note: eval() replaced with mathjs's evaluate() plus try/catch error handling; restricts execution to math grammar, appropriate for a calculator endpoint.

R320.note: Switches FromSqlRaw to EF Core 7+'s parameterizing FromSql interpolated overload and correctly drops the surrounding quotes so tenantId/term bind as parameters, not text; tenant+term filter and async List contract preserved.

R321.note: th:utext -> th:text applies Thymeleaf's context-aware HTML escaping, correctly closing script injection for what is plain-text note content.

R322.note: Sequelize named-placeholder `replacements` correctly parameterizes both dates with identical query semantics.

R323.note: StackExchange.Redis HashSet correctly closes the CRLF/inline-protocol injection, but silently changes SessionNoteWriter's constructor from Socket to IDatabase, a breaking API change for any other caller not addressed or flagged as a migration.

R324.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes replaces the predictable seeded Random; dropping the seed parameter is the necessary consequence of the fix and doesn't affect legitimate clients since query params are otherwise ignored.

R325.note: Ownership-scoping approach is correct, but the delivered loadProjectExport calls an undefined `db.query` (no db import/definition anywhere), so it would throw at runtime for every call rather than working; write-up labels it a 'mock implementation' needing a real query, so the gap is disclosed but not fixed.

R326.note: Restoring self.get_object() reinstates DRF's queryset scoping and object-permission check, giving identical 404s for missing vs. unauthorized invoices as required by the contract.

R327.note: Classic save-next-before-free fix; traversal order, single free per node, and continued iteration after expired nodes are all preserved exactly as the contract requires.

R328.note: Pillow-based content validation, re-encoding, and safe-filename generation correctly close the type-spoofing bypass, but moving storage from static/uploads to a non-static uploads/ directory breaks any existing direct-URL access to the avatar; a replacement serving handler is only gestured at ('serve only through a handler...'), not delivered.

R329.note: Passing the real requestedCapacity into write_field's bound check instead of the oversized constant is exactly the needed one-line fix; matches the stated contract precisely.

R330.note: Replacing the raw socket with JavaMail Session/Transport/MimeMessage plus strict InternetAddress validation closes the CRLF/RCPT injection, but the rewrite also adds mail.smtp.starttls.required=true, a new hard requirement that could break delivery to an internal relay lacking STARTTLS, not flagged as a risk in the write-up.

R331.note: Adds secure=True (closing the reported gap) plus SameSite=Lax; both changes are stated plainly and don't block normal top-level login flows, and the write-up correctly notes the fix assumes HTTPS is enforced site-wide.

R332.note: Loops Read() to fill the full header buffer (or reject as too-small) before comparing signatures, closing the short-read bypass without affecting any file large enough to be a real PNG/PDF.

R333.note: Allowlist of extensions plus MIME-type check is exactly the intended CWE-434 remediation; the type restriction is the point of the fix, stated plainly, not an incidental side effect.

R334.note: Adding the '--' end-of-options marker before user-supplied filenames matches the stated contract, preventing tar option/argument injection while still archiving every filename in order.
